scope: Private browser application source and production-build verification. No registry release, tag or hosted deployment. Constructed damaged audio fixtures, not production incidents or a phonetic accuracy benchmark.

suite.skipScope: Four Firefox microphone cases are excluded because the deterministic test microphone is Chromium-only. No physical microphone or speaker validation is claimed.

fixtureOracle: fixtures.json records independent FFmpeg decoding of all five float WAVE fixtures, including the exact source PCM bytes and non-finite counts.
exportOracle: exports.json records independent FFmpeg decoding of all eight preserved-clip exports. One captured constructed sine-wave export is preserved-clip.wav.
verificationNotes: The clean archive contains the implementation and regression sources. The final evidence driver additionally corrects observation waits and checks saved/playback/export bytes; those changes do not alter compiled application code.

The first probe used the wrong accessible tab name; its rerun used Your attempt. The first replay assumed a zero-valued gap would score 100; native analysis returns 87, so the control requires valid analysis and final before/after score identity. No phonetic target score is invented.

The export failure appears in download-note rather than the general status. The saved-record observer initially read the prior job during Reading. Final captures wait for a new analysis request and its terminal worker result; both baseline and corrected captures were rerun. No application change resolved these harness issues.

Non-finite PCM is rejected in the worker before pitch/spectrogram analysis and clip commit. Lower-level pitch/DTW routines retain their existing partial-signal behavior; 48 valid native controls are bit-identical.
decodeAudioData is still native and cannot be preempted or constrained to a general allocation ceiling. Validation does not certify that an encoded file is intact or that a recording is human speech.
